claims.text: The studied alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten at 1100–1200°C.
Severe lattice distortion is the primary cause of the proposed plastic-strain and toughness improvement in WTaTiVZr.
Random compositional fluctuations and severe lattice distortion can substantially alter dislocation motion in BCC high-entropy alloys.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr creates heterogeneous local stress fields.
Lattice distortion lowers the effective Peierls barrier for dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion activates additional dislocation slip systems in WTaTiVZr.
Severe lattice distortion facilitates dislocation motion.
Dynamic recrystallization can occur in a refractory high-entropy alloy during deformation at 1000–1200°C and can accompany a post-yield flow-stress drop.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr enhances grain-boundary sliding or dynamic recrystallization at 1100–1200°C.
The proposed dislocation and recovery mechanisms produce more spatially uniform plastic deformation.
The proposed dislocation and recovery mechanisms improve crack-tip blunting and toughness.
Pure tungsten has a more uniform lattice, fewer activated slip systems, and consequently more brittle behavior under the same high-temperature conditions.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit lower yield stress than matched pure tungsten at 1100–1200°C.
WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain before failure and improved ductility and toughness relative to matched pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr will show a more homogeneous dislocation distribution, multiple active slip systems, and clearer dynamic-recovery signatures than pure tungsten.
Secondary phases, grain-boundary chemistry, precipitates, and phase instability could govern the mechanical response instead of lattice distortion.
Matching grain size and thermal history and ruling out secondary-phase and grain-boundary differences is sufficient to isolate lattice distortion as the dominant compositional cause.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says severe lattice distortion facilitates dislocation motion by lowering its barrier, whereas the designated conflicting BCC-HEA evidence attributes strengthening and notable difficulty of edge-dislocation movement to severe lattice distortion.
